prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the Z2 topological insulator and the time-reversal-symmetric quantum spin Hall state, and for the first experimental observation of helical edge transport in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B007 as the sole prize part, but with less confidence than in round 1, and the reason is the credit discussion rather than the science. The scientific case has not been challenged by anyone. The Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state are a new organising principle for electronic matter: a bulk gap whose boundary states are protected by time-reversal symmetry and not by symmetry breaking or by an applied magnetic field. That idea turned band-structure analysis into a classification problem, and Z2 and related invariants are now computed routinely in first-principles work on real compounds, which is the part of this field I can judge from daily experience. The Molenkamp group measurement of quantised edge conductance and non-local transport in HgTe wells is the decisive experimental confirmation, and the result has been reproduced and extended for about two decades in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and three-dimensional Bi-based compounds. Maturity is therefore not in doubt. I also accept the chair's request to say what wording makes the novelty relative to 2016 explicit: the citation should name the Z2 invariant and time-reversal-symmetric helical edge states, and should not use the words topological phase transitions or the quantum Hall effect, which belong to the 2016 citation. On the chair's questions, I do think the lattice clock is distinct from combs and ion control, so I do not rest my preference on a novelty objection to B056.
statement.case_against: The attribution problem is real and I now weigh it more heavily than I did in round 1. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal identified HgTe and the critical well thickness, so the Molenkamp experiment was guided by it, and my statement that this is a regrettable but tolerable gap deserves a harder test. Zhang died in 2018, so no configuration can honour him, and the three-dimensional work of Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan and others also sits outside the names. The tolerable-gap argument rests on the claim that the concept and the invariant are Kane and Mele's and that the observation is Molenkamp's. If the committee concludes that the BHZ proposal is part of the discovery and not a material-specific application of it, I would not defend B007 and would move to B056. Second, only two of eight members prefer B007 and six prefer B056, so I must ask whether my ordering reflects a scientific judgement or my proximity to the subject. Third, practical impact on devices is still limited, though that is not a criterion for a discovery prize.

responses.point: Pearce argues that the BHZ proposal guided the HgTe experiment, that Zhang's death in 2018 means the history cannot be repaired by adding him, and that together with the 2016 prize this makes B007 harder to defend publicly than the lattice clock, where credit divides naturally between concept and performance.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my position and I concede part of it. Zhang's death is not repairable and the HgTe route was specific enough that the experiment was not blind. Where I still differ is that the three-name list does not have to claim the HgTe proposal: the Kane-Mele theory and the first observation of helical edge transport are separable achievements that the citation can describe truthfully. But I accept that this is a defensible position and not a clean one, and that a public reader may reasonably find the omission of the proposal that selected the material harder to accept than the omission of Ludlow and Lemonde from the clock prize. That is why the chair's question about indispensability is the one that decides my vote.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the lattice clock, with uncertainty near 1e-18 confirmed by several independent laboratories, is mature, has no forced third name, and that the lattice trap is a different physical mechanism from the 2005 comb and the 2012 ion control.
responses.response: I accept the physical distinction and withdraw the suggestion from round 1 that the clock merely extends the 2005 and 2012 line. Removing the trapping Stark shift with a magic wavelength while keeping many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime is a distinct invention, and agreement between independent clocks is the kind of confirmation I value. My remaining disagreement is on what counts as the larger scientific consequence. I weigh a new classification of electronic matter above a better instrument, but that is a weighting and not a fact, and I will not pretend it outweighs a clearer credit. I also note your own caveat that the concept-versus-performance division between Katori and Ye is partly intertwined, so the cleaner credit of B056 is somewhat less clean than the supporters say.

responses.point: Danielsson argues that the 2016 overlap is not merely procedural because Kane-Mele extends the conceptual line honoured in 2016, so B007 is somewhat less original than it appears, and that if the committee wants a condensed-matter prize the twistronics case pairs theory and experiment more cleanly.
responses.response: I disagree on both points. The Haldane and Thouless-Kosterlitz recognition covers topological phase transitions and the quantum Hall type invariant that requires broken time-reversal symmetry. The Kane-Mele Z2 classification needs time-reversal symmetry and spin-orbit coupling and has a different invariant, different edge physics and different materials, so I regard it as a new step and not an extension, provided the citation says so. On twistronics, I agree the theory-experiment arc is attractive, but the superconducting pairing mechanism and the phase diagram are not settled, and experimental credit is shared with Cao, Dean, Young and Yacoby, so the attribution is no cleaner than B007. I would keep B012 as a later-year candidate.

responses.point: Olsson, who shares my preference for B007, says the three-name limit cannot give a fair attribution if the HgTe proposal is judged indispensable, and that the clock needs only the two originators while later implementers are the normal tail of a prize.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of your argument and want to state explicitly where I would stop. I think the committee owes the public one clear judgement: either BHZ is a platform proposal downstream of Kane-Mele, in which case the trio is defensible, or it is part of the discovery, in which case no three-name list is acceptable and we should not pretend that a citation can fix it. I lean to the first reading but cannot document it from the files, and I recall the sequence from general knowledge. If the committee reads it the second way, I would move to B056 and not hold a split of two members against six.

responses.point: Mehlig keeps B007 as a first alternative, says the 2016 prize leaves room for a second topological award provided the committee judges that openly, and would support B007 if the credit problem is judged tolerable.
responses.response: I agree that the 2016 question is a judgement the committee should make openly and I have tried to do that by proposing citation wording that excludes the 2016 vocabulary. Your conditional support is useful because it shows that the real obstacle is the credit and not the science, and it suggests that the committee could converge on either B007 or B056 depending on one factual and ethical judgement about BHZ. I do not want to argue for B007 beyond what that judgement supports, and I would rather our votes follow from it than from counts of first places.

responses.point: Johansson proposes a two-part prize pairing the lattice clock with Hosono's iron-based superconductors, using three names, and concedes that the two parts have almost nothing in common and that Hosono has thin support.
responses.response: I considered this because it answers the chair's question about a second part, but I do not support it. A second part chosen because it fits the three-name limit is a design for the limit and not a scientific reason. Hosono's discovery is mature and the credit is clean, and I ranked it fourth in the opening, but the shared prize would honour two unrelated results to avoid a credit dispute, and a single achievement is a better public statement. I also see no combination that includes B007 or B056 with another candidate and fits within three names, so I remain with a single part.

uncertainties: Whether the BHZ proposal for HgTe is judged indispensable to the Molenkamp observation; this is the one factual judgement that would move me to B056, and I am recalling the sequence from general knowledge and not from a documented source.
Whether the citation wording can make the novelty of the Z2 invariant and time-reversal-symmetric helical edge relative to the 2016 prize unmistakable.
Whether my weighting of conceptual consequence above instrument performance reflects scientific judgement or proximity to condensed-matter theory.
Whether to wait for the SI redefinition of the second before awarding B056; I regard it as a consequence and not a bar, but I have no special expertise in metrology.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented personal or institutional link to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye, or the twisted bilayer graphene candidates, and I find no recusal trigger in my own record. My field of first-principles electronic structure and magnetism is professionally close to B007, and I have tried to treat that as a reason for scrutiny and not as authority. On the flags raised by others, I support recusal of Johansson from any vote on B058 and see no need for Kroll to step back on B056 on the basis of a doctoral-period stay in the laboratory of a 2005 laureate, though he should keep disclosing it.
